problem_motivation.content: Dose efficiency, not spatial resolution, is now the main limitation of TEM.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: its limiting factor is no longer spatial resolution but dose efficiency

problem_motivation.content: Low-dose imaging creates noisy images without ground truth, making learning difficult.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Low electron doses avoid sample damage but produce noisy images for which, unlike in classical computer vision, there is no ground truth.

problem_motivation.content: Autonomous materials experimentation needs representations tied to microscope state during acquisition.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Autonomous materials experimentation poses a related problem, since closed-loop instruments need representations grounded in the microscope state at acquisition.

problem_motivation.content: Both applications require representations grounded in image acquisition.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Both demand representations grounded in how an image was acquired.

problem_motivation.content: What is missing is an encoder aligning visual content with instrument physical parameters
problem_motivation.evidence_span: In both modes, the missing piece is an encoder that aligns visual content with the physical parameters of the instrument.

problem_motivation.content: Existing TEM data are rarely shared because data-sharing culture is not established
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Unfortunately, this data is almost never shared as the culture of data sharing is not established in the electron microscopy community [Ivanova et al., 2025].

problem_motivation.content: Very little HAADF-STEM data is open-sourced despite large volumes being collected.
problem_motivation.evidence_span:
While petabytes of
HAADF-STEM images are collected each year [Ivanova
et al., 2025], very few are ever open-sourced.

problem_motivation.content: Existing datasets do not provide the scale of paired experimental HAADF-STEM images with rich instrument metadata needed by the paper.
problem_motivation.evidence_span:
None of these match the scale of pairing between
experimental HAADF-STEM images and rich instrument metadata that we target.

problem_motivation.content: No prior work has applied this kind of contrastive image-annotation framework to electron microscopy.
problem_motivation.evidence_span:
To our knowledge, however, no prior
work applies this or any similar framework to electron microscopy (EM).

problem_motivation.content: Lower electron doses create a constant need for denoisers that make low-dose data interpretable.
problem_motivation.evidence_span:
With those ever diminishing electron doses, the need for appropriate denoisers
to make low-dose data interpretable and easy to use, is constant.

problem_motivation.content: There are no general STEM denoisers informed by acquisition settings and pixel size that work across instrument settings.
problem_motivation.evidence_span:
As far as the authors are aware, there exist no general STEM denoisers in
the sense that they are informed about the acquisition settings and pixel size related to the images and
can produce good results across instrument settings.

problem_motivation.content: A factored representation grounded in physical microscope state is needed for autonomous high-throughput microscopy.
problem_motivation.evidence_span:
A
factored representation grounded in physical microscope state is a foundational requirement for any
such system

problem_motivation.content: Training data lacks examples of extreme acquisition boundary conditions, leaving those behaviors unlearned.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Boundary conditions are missing from the training data.

problem_motivation.content: Although large for this microscopy niche, the dataset is still small and narrow compared with computer-vision datasets.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: It is nonetheless modest and narrow by computer-vision standards

Prior work has applied image-to-image

And in another work, Lobato et al. [2024] train

prior_approach.content: Self-supervised denoisers such as Noise2Noise, Noise2Void, and UDVD have been popular for STEM denoising.

Self-supervised denoisers in the
Noise2Noise / Noise2Void / UDVD family [Lehtinen et al., 2018, Krull et al., 2019, Sheth et al., 2021]

prior_approach.content: GAN-based denoisers including Noise2Atom have also been explored.
prior_approach.evidence_span:
GAN-based denoisers have also been explored.
Noise2Atom [Wang et al., 2020] is an unsupervised GAN-based denoiser trained on noisy acquisitions

with which it was trained.

prior_limitation.content: Existing experimental datasets are small, narrow in material coverage, and usually lack acquisition metadata needed for generalization across settings.
prior_limitation.evidence_span:
Existing exper-
imental datasets tend to be small, narrow in material coverage, and rarely include the acquisition
metadata needed to train models that generalise across instrument settings.

prior_limitation.content: These previous image-to-image approaches are one-to-one and agnostic to microscope settings.
prior_limitation.evidence_span:
These approaches are all
one-to-one and agnostic to microscope settings (i.e., a dedicated network is trained per source/target
domain pair, with no natural way to parameterise the target style).

prior_limitation.content: Prior methods require retraining a new CycleGAN for each dwell time or detector gain setting.
prior_limitation.evidence_span:
Simulating a different dwell time
or detector gain with any previous method requires training a new CycleGAN with a new paired or
unpaired corpus at that setting.

prior_limitation.content: These denoisers are heavily specialized to single noise profiles and materials, and some require paired time-series data.
prior_limitation.evidence_span:
However, these models are heavily specialised
for single noise profiles and materials samples, some of which (such as Noise2Noise) further require
time-series data where noise changes but image content does not (i.e., true image pairs).

prior_limitation.content: Noise2Void-based methods can introduce checkerboard artifacts and lose detail when pixels are not much smaller than atomic features.
prior_limitation.evidence_span:
Noise2Void-
based techniques that can work on single or unpaired images instead introduce checkerboard artefacts
when trained to convergence and lose image detail if pixel size is not significantly smaller than the
atomic features the experimentalist is interested in.

prior_limitation.content: The model fails to capture the clipping boundary condition seen experimentally for gain changes.
prior_limitation.evidence_span:
However,
it does not successfully model the boundary condition where the experimental image is clipped.

prior_limitation.content: Noise2Void is overly aggressive, shows checkerboard artifacts, and hallucinates background content by smoothing speckle noise into gaussians.
prior_limitation.evidence_span:
which is overly aggressive in its denoising, suffers from checkerboard artifacts
(Figure 2), and tends to hallucinate content in background regions by smoothing speckle noise into
gaussians.

prior_limitation.content: The current corpus cannot support the model scaling seen in larger vision datasets.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: and has supported three orders of magnitude of model scaling beyond what our corpus can support.

rejected_alternative.content: Rather than one-to-one setting-agnostic methods, the paper uses a one-to-many generator conditioned on continuous acquisition metadata so target settings can be queried without retraining.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span:
The style-transfer network we present downstream of CIMP
is instead one-to-many: a single generator is conditioned on continuous acquisition metadata through CIMP
embeddings such that any target instrument setting can be queried at inference without retraining.

rejected_alternative.content: Methods dominated by iterative refinement are ruled out because they are too slow for real-time use.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span:
This rules out methods whose inference cost is
dominated by iterative refinement.

rejected_alternative.content: Palette-style diffusion was not used because it requires paired source-target examples unavailable here.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span:
By contrast, Palette-style image-to-image diffusion [Saharia et al.,
2021] requires paired source-target examples that we do not have

rejected_alternative.content: Flow matching was not used because it is naturally noise-to-image rather than metadata-conditioned image-to-image translation.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span:
and flow matching [Lipman et al.,
2022] is natively a noise-to-image generative method rather than an image-to-image translator that
can be conditioned on metadata.

rejected_alternative.content: Pixel size was excluded from qualitative style-transfer evaluation because changing field of view synthetically at fixed image dimensions has no physical basis.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span:
We qualitatively evaluate style transfer for each metadata parameter individually, with the exception
of pixel size. Since pixel size is determined by the image’s field of view, altering it synthetically
while keeping image dimensions fixed has no physical basis

rejected_alternative.content: Noise2Atom was excluded from the user study because it was not considered a comparable denoiser.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span:
We therefore do not
consider Noise2Atom a comparable denoiser and exclude it from the user study below.

inspiration_source.content: The method is inspired by or derived from CLIP-style training
inspiration_source.evidence_span: we propose Contrastive Image-Metadata Pre-training (CIMP), a CLIP-style method [Radford et al., 2021]

inspiration_source.content: The approach is structurally analogous to CLOOME in microscopy.
inspiration_source.evidence_span:
The closest structural ana-
logue in any microscopy domain is CLOOME [Sanchez-Fernandez et al., 2023], which contrastively
aligns fluorescence cell-painting images with chemical-structure embeddings and demonstrates
cross-modal retrieval across a large bioimaging database.

inspiration_source.content: The approach is conceptually parallel to ContIG, which aligns images with structured physical annotations.
inspiration_source.evidence_span:
ContIG [Taleb et al., 2022] is the closest
conceptual parallel: a medical-imaging model that contrastively aligns retinal images with a structured
physical-annotation vector (SNP arrays, polygenic risk scores).

causal_claim.content: Using the embedding to condition a metadata-conditioned style-transfer model enables re-rendering under different acquisition parameters.
causal_claim.evidence_span: we use the embedding to condition a metadata-conditioned style-transfer model that re-renders experimental images under different acquisition parameters

causal_claim.content: Virtually scaling dwell time and beam current converts the model into a physics-informed denoiser.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Virtually scaling dwell time and beam current of low-dose images turns this model into a physics-informed denoiser

causal_claim.content: Limiting electron dose causes images to become very noisy
causal_claim.evidence_span: Limiting the electron dose is crucial to avoid sample damage and ensure physical relevance of observed phenomena, but naturally leads to very noisy images

causal_claim.content: TEM experiment exploration and tuning cause large amounts of data to remain unused
causal_claim.evidence_span: Yet, for every published image, a massive volume of data, more than 90% by some estimates [Ivanova et al., 2025], remains unused, not because the quality of the data is bad but because TEM experiments require exploration and tuning to identify and record the golden data that eventually makes publication.

causal_claim.content: Using the embedding as perceptual loss and conditioning enables style transfer across acquisition parameters
causal_claim.evidence_span: we use the embedding as both a perceptual loss and a conditioning signal for a generative metadata-conditioned style-transfer model that translates an experimental image into the style it would have had under different acquisition parameters

causal_claim.content: Virtually scaling dwell time and beam current allows the style-transfer model to act as a physics-informed denoiser
causal_claim.evidence_span: we use the style-transfer model as a physics-informed denoiser by virtually scaling dwell time and beam current of low-dose images

causal_claim.content: Contrastive image-metadata alignment yields a factored, physics-aligned representation as a byproduct of retrieval training.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
Yet seven physically distinct acquisition pa-
rameters are independently recoverable from the frozen 128-d embedding through a closed-form
linear probe, evidence that contrastive image-metadata alignment yields a factored, physics-aligned
representation as a byproduct of retrieval training.

causal_claim.content: These constraints motivate using a GAN-based architecture.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
These constraints
motivate a GAN-based architecture.

causal_claim.content: This indicates the model changes images by about as much as natural changes between adjacent real acquisitions.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
This indicates that the
CIMP GAN modifies the input by an amount comparable to the natural change between adjacent
real acquisitions in the series.

causal_claim.content: Gain appears to be modeled most actively, while dwell has the highest baseline similarity because adjacent dwell-series images differ only modestly.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
Among the three series, the CIMP GAN’s similarity to the reference is
highest for gain, suggesting the model captures the gain change most actively, while dwell shows the
highest baseline similarity since consecutive images in the dwell series differ only modestly to begin
with.

causal_claim.content: Together, the image-level and distributional results indicate the model reproduces experimental changes with realistic magnitude and distribution.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
Read together,
Tables 2 and 3 indicate that the CIMP GAN reproduces the experimental change at both the per-image
and the distributional level, with the magnitude of induced change matching the natural intra-series
variation and the output distribution matching the distribution of real eval-set images.

causal_claim.content: Increasing dwell time makes generated images smoother but also brightens the background unlike experiments.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
In general, increasing dwell time does make the image smoother as expected, but
also makes the background brighter, which does not happen in the experimental series.

causal_claim.content: Virtually increasing dwell time and beam current lets the model be used as a denoiser.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
Finally, we utilize the CIMP-conditioned GAN model as a denoiser by feeding it a target embedding
etgt derived from the source metadata with virtually increased dwell time and beam current.

causal_claim.content: Noise2Void behaves like a low-pass filter, strongly suppressing high frequencies while leaving low frequencies mostly unchanged.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
Noise2Void shows a simple low-pass profile, suppressing high-frequency power by
roughly an order of magnitude while leaving low frequencies essentially unchanged.

causal_claim.content: CIMP GAN suppresses power gently and almost uniformly across frequencies.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
Our CIMP GAN
suppresses power gently and almost uniformly across the spectrum

causal_claim.content: Noise2Atom adds low-to-mid-frequency power while suppressing high frequencies.
causal_claim.evidence_span:
Noise2Atom suppresses
high-frequency content but adds power in the low-to-mid frequency range

causal_claim.content: Under-representation of parameter extremes causes the model to miss corresponding image behaviors.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As a result, the upper and lower bounds of each acquisition parameter are under-represented in the dataset, and the model has no examples from which to learn the corresponding image behaviours.

mechanism_principle.content: Unused data arises from the exploratory and tuning-heavy nature of TEM experiments rather than poor data quality
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: not because the quality of the data is bad but because TEM experiments require exploration and tuning to identify and record the golden data that eventually makes publication

mechanism_principle.content: Open-sourcing is limited because publications emphasize only the best images and data-sharing culture is weak.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
Mi-
croscopy publications typically focus on findings from
the highest-quality images, and the culture of data shar-
ing is not well-established in the field.

mechanism_principle.content: This suggests HAADF-STEM-specific image priors are needed because natural-image and atomic-scale image distributions differ.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
which conveys the need for HAADF-STEM
image priors given the difference in distributions between natural images and atomic-scale images.

mechanism_principle.content: SMAPE is inflated for the log-transformed wide-range variables because residuals are re-exponentiated from log10 space.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
The three log10-transformed di-
mensions with wide dynamic range (pixel
size, dwell time, beam current) show in-
flated SMAPE of 28–47% despite R2 ∈
[0.66, 0.78], reflecting the multiplicative ef-
fect of re-exponentiating log10-space resid-
uals.

mechanism_principle.content: GANs are suitable because they allow one-shot inference, work on small datasets, fit the LPIPS-based objective, and do not require true pairs.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
GANs admit one-shot inference without iterative ODE solving,
train reliably on small datasets, integrate naturally with the multi-task LPIPS-based objective we use,
and allow us to jointly optimise for the correct metadata style, content preservation, and image realism
without true image-metadata pairs.

mechanism_principle.content: The common KID around 0.19 versus training data reflects content shift between eval-series and training corpus rather than model artifacts.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
Against the training corpus, the CIMP GAN’s KID (0.185) matches the content-gap floor
(0.189) within one standard error. The common ∼0.19 value therefore reflects the shift between the
narrow eval-series content and the wider training distribution, not a model artefact.

mechanism_principle.content: Poor offset performance is likely caused by limited diversity in the training set.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This is likely due to limited diversity in the training set.

mechanism_principle.content: This frequency behavior is consistent with denoising via metadata-driven style shift rather than frequency cutoff.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
consistent with its denoising
mechanism being a metadata-driven style shift rather than a frequency cutoff.

mechanism_principle.content: This happens because Noise2Atom imprints periodic atomic-lattice content regardless of the actual sample.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
reflecting the periodic
atomic-lattice content the model imprints on every input regardless of the underlying sample.

mechanism_principle.content: Extreme parameter behaviors are not learned because operators avoid recording bad clipped or saturated images.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Operators do not routinely record images with clipped intensities, saturated detectors, or other extreme boundary conditions, because such acquisitions are considered bad.

hypothesis_statement.content: The proposed CIMP method aligns images with acquisition metadata.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: propose Contrastive Image-Metadata Pre-training (CIMP), a CLIP-style encoder that aligns the two modalities

hypothesis_statement.content: For downstream conditioning, the embedding should encode physically meaningful microscope-state axes, not just retrieval cues.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span:
For CIMP embeddings to serve as a foundation layer that downstream models can condition on,
the representation must encode physically meaningful axes of microscope state, not just enough
information to re-pair an image with its own metadata at retrieval time.

hypothesis_statement.content: Future improvement will come from collecting a larger and more diverse dataset from additional facilities.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Future work will include amassing a higher volume and more diverse corpus of data from further research facilities.

evidence_result.content: CIMP achieves strong cross-modal retrieval performance on held-out data.
evidence_result.evidence_span: reaches 84.4% Top-1 cross-modal retrieval on a held-out split

evidence_result.content: All acquisition parameters can be linearly recovered from the frozen visual embedding.
evidence_result.evidence_span: All seven parameters are individually recoverable from the frozen visual embedding through a linear probe

evidence_result.content: Microscopists preferred the method over the current state-of-the-art denoiser in most trials.
evidence_result.evidence_span: in a blind user study, experimental microscopists prefer it over the current state-of-the-art denoiser for STEM imagery on 70.2% of trials

evidence_result.content: CIMP reaches 84.4% Top-1 cross-modal retrieval on held-out validation data
evidence_result.evidence_span: reaching Top-1 cross-modal retrieval of 84.4% on a held-out validation split

evidence_result.content: Linear probing recovers all seven acquisition parameters from the frozen visual embedding
evidence_result.evidence_span: linear probing shows that all seven acquisition parameters are individually recoverable from the frozen 128-d visual embedding through Ridge regression despite the contrastive objective never supervising any metadata value directly

evidence_result.content: Microscopists preferred the denoiser over Noise2Void in 70.2% of trials
evidence_result.evidence_span: In a blind user study, experimental microscopists prefer this denoiser over the state-of-the-art Noise2Void baseline on 70.2% of trials.

evidence_result.content: The dataset introduced contains 7,330 HAADF-STEM images with paired metadata over more than 30 material systems and 130 samples.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
In this work, we introduce 7,330 HAADF-STEM images with paired metadata from a Titan mi-
croscope at an anonymised materials-research laboratory. The dataset covers more than 30 distinct
materials systems, predominantly heterogeneous catalysts (Pt/CeO2, Pd/ZrO2, Ru/TiO2, In2O3/ZrO2,
etc.), with more than 130 material samples synthesized by different techniques and with different
metal loading, imaged with a variety of instrument settings.

evidence_result.content: Special evaluation sets were collected as true experimental image series varying one metadata parameter at a time.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
We additionally solicited the creation of several evaluation sets,

which are series of true experimental images captured of the same sample in quick succession while
varying a single metadata parameter. These series sweep dwell time, gain, and offset respectively.

evidence_result.content: The chosen CIMP configuration achieved Top-1 0.8438, Top-5 0.9688, and Top-10 0.9844 on held-out validation.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
We train for 1000 epochs and achieve final Top-1 of 0.8438, Top-5 of 0.9688,
and Top-10 of 0.9844 on our held-out validation set.

evidence_result.content: All seven metadata parameters are linearly decodable from the frozen 128-d embedding.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
All seven metadata parameters are lin-
early decodable from the frozen 128-d em-
bedding (Table 1).

evidence_result.content: Correct output-target pairs exceed incorrect pairs by 0.523 cosine similarity, showing conditioning aligns generated style with the target embedding.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
As shown in Figure 7, the mean similarity of correct
pairs exceeds that of incorrect pairs by 0.523 on the cosine-similarity scale (bounded in [−1, 1]),
demonstrating that the generator aligns image style with the provided conditioning embedding.

evidence_result.content: Style-transfer fidelity metrics are very close to the real evaluation-series baseline.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
Table 2 shows that the SSIM, PSNR, and LPIPS values are very consistent between
the CIMP GAN and the eval-series baseline across all three series, with the two rows differing by
less than 0.02 on SSIM, 1.3 on PSNR, and 0.05 on LPIPS in every case.

evidence_result.content: The model's KID against real eval-set images is near zero, indicating close distributional match.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
Most
directly, the CIMP GAN’s KID against the real eval-set images is near zero (−0.016 ± 0.009), and
we conclude that its output distribution almost perfectly matches the distribution of the real evaluation
images.

evidence_result.content: For gain, the model correctly predicts brightness changes when gain is lowered or increased.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
For gain, our
model correctly predicts the behaviour of lowering and increasing brightness in the image.

evidence_result.content: The model performs worst on offset, with little generated variation despite substantial experimental change.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
The
CIMP-conditioned GAN model performs worst on the offset parameter; there is almost no difference
between generated images across offset values, though the experimental series shows substantial
change.

evidence_result.content: Qualitatively, the CIMP GAN denoiser gives more realistic outputs than Noise2Void.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
Qualitatively, our CIMP GAN denoiser consistently outputs more realistic looking denoised images
than Noise2Void

evidence_result.content: Noise2Atom fails broadly, collapsing content when the input is not a clean atomic lattice.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
Noise2Atom fails on the broader denoising task, with complete content
collapse on any input whose content is not a clean atomic-resolution lattice.

evidence_result.content: Quantitatively, CIMP GAN preserves the most edge magnitude among compared denoisers.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
Our CIMP GAN preserves the
most edge magnitude (edge energy ratio 0.79).

evidence_result.content: Noise2Void preserves edge locations best but retains only 36% of edge magnitude due to aggressive smoothing.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
Noise2Void preserves edge location best (gradient
correlation 0.69) but smooths aggressively and retains only 36% of total edge magnitude.

evidence_result.content: Noise2Atom scores poorly on both edge metrics because it collapses images onto an atomic prior.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
Noise2Atom
collapses image content onto a learned atomic prior, scoring poorly on both edge metrics.

evidence_result.content: In the blind user study, CIMP GAN was chosen in 70.2% of trials, significantly above chance.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
Across all 486 judgments, CIMP GAN is chosen on 70.2% (Wilson 95% CI [66.0, 74.1]) of trials,
significantly above 50% (binomial p < 10−3).

evidence_result.content: Most raters preferred CIMP GAN, though one rater was at chance.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
Per-rater preference is uneven, four raters prefer
CIMP at 68–86% while one is indistinguishable from chance at 50.7% (Table 5).

evidence_result.content: Raters reported that Noise2Void produced sharper but less realistic images with cross artifacts and worked better when raw signal was already high.
evidence_result.evidence_span:
A general impression from some of the
raters was that "the one with cross artefacts" (N2V) generates sharper but more unrealistic images,
and works better when the signal of the raw image is already quite high.

evidence_result.content: The gain sweep shows the model captures brighter/noisier trends but not saturation at high values.
evidence_result.evidence_span: This is visible in the gain sweep (Figure 5b), where the model correctly reproduces the trend of increasing brightness and noise but fails to saturate at the high end

evidence_result.content: Extreme offset values are reproduced poorly.
evidence_result.evidence_span: and in the offset sweep (Figure 5c), where extreme values are poorly reproduced.

constraint.content: Electron dose must be limited to avoid sample damage and preserve physical relevance

constraint.content: Autonomous TEM systems require image representations grounded in the microscope state at acquisition
constraint.evidence_span: any such autonomous system needs a representation of each image grounded in the instrument state under which it was acquired

constraint.content: The main corpus has no paired or matched source-target groupings, only varied unpaired samples across acquisition parameters.

problem_motivation.content: In transmission electron microscopy/electron microscopy, dose efficiency has become the main limitation rather than spatial resolution: lowering electron dose avoids sample damage but produces noisy images without ground truth, creating a constant need for denoisers that make low-dose data interpretable.
evidence_spans: its limiting factor is no longer spatial resolution but dose efficiency
Low electron doses avoid sample damage but produce noisy images for which, unlike in classical computer vision, there is no ground truth.
With those ever diminishing electron doses, the need for appropriate denoisers to make low-dose data interpretable and easy to use, is constant.

problem_motivation.content: Autonomous materials experimentation and closed-loop microscopy require representations grounded in image acquisition and physical microscope state; more specifically, a factored encoder/representation is needed that aligns visual content with instrument parameters at acquisition.
evidence_spans: Autonomous materials experimentation poses a related problem, since closed-loop instruments need representations grounded in the microscope state at acquisition.
Both demand representations grounded in how an image was acquired.
In both modes, the missing piece is an encoder that aligns visual content with the physical parameters of the instrument.
A factored representation grounded in physical microscope state is a foundational requirement for any such system
